title: Factory
about: A body of work's repositories, workflows and hires.

terms.meaning: a named grouping in the store: the repositories a body of work is on, the workflows it offers and the repository each works on, and the agents it hires into their steps.

the count of changes to a factory's spec, Kubernetes' `metadata.generation`, kept on its file as `generation`: filed at 1, one more for each write through the Factory door that changes its repositories, workflows, hires, volumes, harness settings, revisions policy, template or level, none for a schedule or its instruction's place (`generationAfter`, proved by `packages/agent-orchestrator/contracts/generation.contract.ts`, in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/factory/door/generation.ts`). A file written before the counter reads as 1. The controller writes the generation it read as the status's `observedGeneration`.

a folder of the person's machine a factory mounts for every local step of its runs, beside its repositories, marked read-only (`:ro`) or writable (`:rw`) as docker compose marks one; kept in the factory's own file, never in its template. A writable one is writable only where a step's fence writes, and is not the run's workspace: nothing commits or lands what a step writes there.

the name a factory's volume is served and linked under, stored on its entry at `nemia factory volume add`: its folder's name as a slug (`volumeBase`), with a suffix, `<base>-2`, where another volume of the factory holds it (`volumeNameAmong`, proved by `packages/agent-orchestrator/contracts/volume-name.contract.ts`). An entry an older file stores none of is named on read, after the stored names, in path order (`volumesNamed`, `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/factory/volume/volume.ts`); a name once stored is kept.

the one repository of its factory a workflow's runs work on, named by the repository's folder name in the factory's wiring (`workflowRepos`, `nemia factory attach <f> <wf> --repo <name>`), else the factory's only repository; a factory of several that names none for a workflow, or names one none or two of its repositories have, refuses the start (`workflowRepo`, proved by `packages/agent-orchestrator/contracts/workflow-repo.contract.ts`, in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/factory/factory.ts`). A card's and a brief's run are placed by it alone, never by the card, the folder a start is typed in nor the daemon's. Kept in the factory's own file, or in its tree's wiring where it is made from a template, as an attach writes it. No verb adds a repository to a factory today: one that does names a repository for each workflow it leaves unwired.

the settings of a harness a factory gives every session of its runs' steps on it, on top of the repository's own: for Claude Code, through the Agent SDK's settings option, never a file written into the repository. A factory sets `attribution`, `includeGitInstructions` and `language` alone, each changing what a session writes or says and none what it may reach or run; kept in the factory's own file, never in its template, and frozen on a run at its start.

the one way a factory is read and written — its file, and the level, rules and servers the store keeps beside it: `FactoryDoor` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/factory/door/factories.store.ts`, its files layer at the store's root a program is given and a memory one, each refusing a write that breaks the model's `Factory`.

a person's change of what a factory offers, hires and schedules — attach, detach, hire, fire, schedule, unschedule — judged by `wiringRefusal` and applied by `rewired` (`packages/agent-orchestrator/src/factory/wiring/wiring.ts`), whose contract proves that a change which would hire or schedule outside the factory's offer is refused; the door's decode through the model `Factory` refuses a factory written that does.

which condition the controller says of a factory made from a template: `Applied`, whether its base holds the template, or `ConflictsPending`, whether an upgrade waits on a person's choice. Its status is `True` or `False`, and the sentence a person reads is its `message`; written by `condition` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/factory/applied/applied.verb.ts`.

why a factory's condition holds or not, one word: `Rendered`, `Upgraded`, `TemplateInvalid`, `VersionDrift`, `ParamsChanged`, `ContentChanged`, `VersionUnknown` or `UpgradePending` for `Applied`; `NoUpgrade`, `Merged` or `Conflicts` for `ConflictsPending`. A status file holding another word reads as none, and the next pass writes it again; the sentence is its `message`.

when a templated factory's condition last moved, `lastTransitionTime` on each condition of its status file, as Kubernetes' SetStatusCondition keeps it: kept while its status holds, stamped with the pass's time where its status flips, where the condition is new, and where a status written before the field kept none; a reason or a message that changes moves no time (`transitionedAt`, proved by `packages/agent-orchestrator/contracts/condition-time.contract.ts`, in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/factory/applied/condition-time.ts`).
a factory's name: its file's in the store, without its extension, a lowercase slug of at most 40 characters.
what Nemia is to know about a factory, `NEMIA.md` by default; no step is told it.
the rules and policies of one factory, a file kept in your store with it, `~/.agent-workflows/factories/<name>/RULES.md`, told to every agent hired into it.

whether a factory's runs follow merged revisions, `follow`, each new filing taking the workflow, agents, skills and rules the files hold then, or stay `pinned`, the default, keeping what they resolved until `nemia refresh`.
a factory's choice of the agent that does one step of a workflow.

a factory made portable: a folder whose manifest, nemia.yaml, declares its version, parameters and hires, beside its workflows, agents and skills, or an archive of one `nemia template pack` wrote; keyed by its source, as `Template` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/template/door/templates.model.ts`.
where a template is read from: its folder or its archive, by its whole path, checked when a template is written and read by name alone, so a factory's file written before the check still reads.

the one way a template's folder or archive is read, written and packed: `TemplateDoor` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/template/door/templates.store.ts`, rooted as the Factory door is, its files layer and a memory one, each refusing a tree whose name or paths `TemplateTreeWrite` refuses. The template's lint is the verbs', not the door's.

the template a factory was made from by `nemia factory apply`, or taken over by `nemia factory adopt`, as its file records it under `template`: the template's source (a folder or archive by its whole path, or the name of a builtin template, resolved on every read), the version the factory wants, and the parameters given with `--set`.

a factory made by hand taken over in place by a template: `nemia factory diff <name> --template …` previews it as a plan with its digest, and `nemia factory adopt … --plan <digest>` writes it, the render staged as the factory's base and tree and the template named in its file; its name, repositories, schedules, instruction, cards, runs and stats stay. The plan is `AdoptPlan`, judged by `adoptRefusal` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/adopt/adopt.ts`.

an upgrade of a factory onto a template of another name than the one its base was rendered from (the template's own `metadata.name`, never its source): the factory's tree and the new render merge with no common base, by `switchTrees` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/factory/upgrade/merge.ts`, chosen by `mergeBaseOf` beside it. A file both hold alike is clean, a file only the template holds is added, and a file only the tree holds, or each run of lines that differs, is a conflict for the person; it is always filed with its plan's `--plan`, and the new render is the base later upgrades merge three ways from.

see.label: Moving onto sdlc from another template

terms.meaning: a template that comes with Nemia: a folder holding its nemia.yaml in the templates workspace (`packages/templates/<name>`), found by path from the orchestrator's own folder (`BUILTIN_TEMPLATES` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/template/door/templates.store.ts`) and never imported; named by its folder's name alone at `--template` and on a factory's file, where `templatePlace` resolves it on every read.

`${{ parameters.<name> }}`, written in a template's text: a render writes it with the parameter's value in every string of a document and in every text it writes — a step's and an agent's instructions, NEMIA.md, RULES.md (`substitute` and `interpolated` in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/factory/applied/params.ts`) — and copies a carried file (a script, a skill's files, a schema) byte for byte; `nemia template lint` refuses a name nemia.yaml does not declare (`packages/agent-orchestrator/src/template/check.ts`). A shell's `$VAR` and `${VAR}` are none.

the factory a run or a card that names none is in, `default` (objects' `DEFAULT_NAMESPACE`): no file, served by the Factory door as a record of its own (`DefaultFactory`, `{ kind: 'default', name: 'default' }`, `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/factory/factory.model.ts`), which a read answers beside a filed factory (`FactoryRecord`) and a write refuses as `Conflict`.

retired.card: run-core, one read of a run (B): the default factory is a record the Factory door serves

terms.meaning: how an upgrade's conflict is resolved: by a proposal of the object that holds its file in the factory's tree, its owner — a file directly in a workflow's folder by that Workflow, an agent's file or result schema by that Agent, a text file of a skill's folder at any depth by that Skill, a step's hire in the wiring (`factory.json#hires.<workflow>/<step>`) by the Hire `<workflow>.<step>`, the rules and the instruction (RULES.md, NEMIA.md) by the Factory itself — carrying it as the choices compose it, which `nemia factory resolve` makes and the factory's resolutions name by the owner's key (`<Kind>/<name>`, a bare name a Workflow's); the pass takes the owner's files from the tree once it applied, and its conflicts wait until then (`UpgradeResolution`, `ResolutionOwner`, `packages/agent-orchestrator/contracts/resolution.contract.ts`). Everything else stays the person's choice: a carried file, in the tree's carried folder, shared by every workflow and code a check runs, which a proposal's access judgement cannot measure, so no object holds it; the wiring's other keys, its revisions policy the person's setting; the wiring whole; a file nested deeper in a workflow's folder; and a file that is not text. A choice that would remove a Skill, the rules or the instruction, which no proposal removes, is refused.

retired.card: factory: an upgrade conflict outside a workflow folder is a proposal of its own kind too, and carried files get a way to be proposed

terms.meaning: a factory's repository named by its git URL: kept in the store under `clones/<host>/<path>` (`cloneTarget`, proved by `packages/agent-orchestrator/contracts/clone-target.contract.ts`, in `packages/agent-orchestrator/src/factory/clones/clones.ts`), its URL recorded beside it in the factory's `origins`, cloned by the place's `clone` when the factory is added or applied, on the api's machine where that is asked over the api (`factories.create`, `factories.apply`), and again by the daemon's sweep when its folder is gone (`clonesOnce`). The machine's own git credentials make it; Nemia holds none.
